newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMU criteria should be taken seriously - Gaddum.
newsitem.headline: EMU criteria should be taken seriously - Gaddum.

text.p: Bundesbank deputy president Johann Gaddum said on Sunday the convergence criteria should be taken seriously but that there was no economic difference between deficits of 2.9 percent or 3.1 percent of economic output.
The new European central bank's monetary policies will be as strong as the Bundesbank's, Gaddum said in a radio interview.

All the Maastricht criteria should be observed according to the treaty, but the treaty says only that deficits should be three percent of gross domestic product (GDP), and that this be sustained over time, Gaddum said.
"The decimal-point discussion has never been a discussion of the Bundesbank's," Gaddum said.
He warned against expectations that the euro would be a magic potion for solving the unemployment situation.
Bavaria's conservative premier Edmund Stoiber last week won a pledge from Chancellor that the deficit rule would be strictly observed as 3.0 percent of GDP.
